audit.whatIsWrong: Two rows flatly contradicted their own whys: win[4] said Trundle while whys[4] ends 'win the side-lane 1v1', and win[6] said K'Sante while whys[6] says the long drain duel slips away. Rows 0 and 1 also disagreed with the packet chart.
audit.why: At 58.55% over 345 games this is K'Sante-favoured through the mid game, and the late is where Trundle's sustain claws back to level.
audit.corrected: Level 1 = Skill (5/10), Level 2 = K'Sante, Level 6 = K'Sante (6/10), 2+ items = Skill (5/10), all in matched pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike was sold as 'duelist-mode penetration' four times.
audit.why: All Out's Riot text grants increased damage, healing and transformed abilities at reduced defenses — there is no penetration. The actual level-6 mechanic worth writing is that R launches the target through ANY wall in its path, including Trundle's own Pillar of Ice.
audit.corrected: Penetration removed from whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[1]; the wall-launch stated instead.
sources: mirrorFindings: All Out launches through any wall, pillar included

audit.whatIsWrong: Q3 was called a knock-up in four places and treated as a third-stack payout. Ntofo Strikes fires its shockwave at TWO stacks and PULLS enemies in. Chomp's auto-reset was also never mentioned.
audit.why: Counting to three means mistiming the payout, and expecting a knock-up when you get a pull means expecting him to be pushed away when he is dragged toward you. Chomp resetting his attack means the wind-up, not the cast, is the cue to step back.
audit.corrected: Two-stack pull written into whys[2], spikes[0], early and wants.you[0]; the auto-reset tell added to wants.foe[0].
sources: kit file: trundle Q autoReset flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentioned Grievous Wounds, and never mentioned that Frozen Domain increases his healing from all sources while he stands on it.
audit.why: King's Tribute heals him off every dying unit and Subjugate steals resistances outright, so more armour is the wrong purchase; and the whole reason 'don't duel him in his W' is true is the healing amp.

edits.before: Level 1 is a coin-flip farm window — you only have Q and no engage, and his Q-bite steals your attack damage so don't trade autos you don't need. The lane swings your way at 3: once W and Q are both up you can W a Trundle who walks in for a pillar or a bite, knock him into terrain for the long stun, and Q3 knock-up before his drain matters. Respect his E pillar — he'll drop it to block your W path or wall you off, so bait it out or angle your dash around it.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coin-flip farm window — you only have Q and no engage, and Chomp steals your attack damage, so don't trade autos you don't need. The lane swings your way at 3: once W and Q are both up you can W a Trundle who walks in for a pillar or a bite, stun him with the knockback, and Q3-pull at two stacks before his drain matters. Respect Pillar of Ice — 21 seconds at rank 1, and he drops it to block your W path, so bait it or angle your dash around it.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are your control peak. You out-trade him around cooldowns: he's a sustain-grind drain-tank with no burst, so your bulk lets you sit in his face and your Passive move-speed keeps you on him. At 6, All Out is the swing — dash through him, and even though it strips your tankiness, Trundle has no burst to punish the lost armor, while your duelist penetration and shred eat through his resists. The one thing to fear is his R: it steals YOUR resistances and heals him, so never commit the all-in while you're low or his ult is up.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 are your control peak. You out-trade him around cooldowns: he's a sustain-grind drain-tank with no burst, so your bulk lets you sit in his face and your Passive move-speed keeps you on him. At 6, All Out is the swing — R launches him through any wall, his own pillar included, and though it strips your tankiness Trundle has no burst to punish the lost armour while your damage boost eats him down. The one thing to fear is Subjugate: it steals YOUR resistances and heals him, so never commit while you're low.

edits.before: This is the only place Trundle reclaims footing — he's a drain-tank built to out-sustain bruisers and tanks in long fights, and his R steal-resists scales into every extended brawl. Your armor stacking does little against a champ whose whole pattern is grinding you down with Q-bite AD theft and lifesteal. So close it on your earlier windows: take side-lane fights at 6 and first item where your All Out and Iceborn disruption win, and don't bet on a 25-minute drain duel where his sustain out-paces your peel.
edits.after: This is the only place Trundle reclaims footing — he's a drain-tank built to out-sustain bruisers in long fights, and Frozen Domain raises his healing from every source while he stands on it, so fighting inside it is the mistake. Grievous Wounds, not more armour, is the answer to King's Tribute and Subjugate. Close it on your earlier windows: take side-lane fights at 6 and first item where your All Out and Iceborn disruption win, and don't bet on a 25-minute drain duel.
